title: mcp.server.ts keeps a module-level let makeAdapter that tests swap through setAdapterFactory and must reset after every case.
evidence: Done 2026-11-13: the adapter factory is an optional makeAdapter field of EndpointWiring (HostedWiring plus makeAdapter, mcp.server.ts), the third argument of mcpEndpoint; with none the endpoint builds REAL_ADAPTER per sealed provider. The two routes (app/routes/mcp.$.tsx:152, :320) call mcpEndpoint(request) only, so no request input can reach it. setAdapterFactory, the module let and every afterEach reset are gone; the six test files pass the factory through their rpc helpers (a file-level const where it never changes, a file-level let set in beforeEach where cases swap it). mcp.hosted-guards.test.ts keeps vi.resetModules (it is what makes the second server instance) but no longer re-sets a seam on it or resets it in a finally. mcp.server.default-adapter.test.ts pins the real default per provider at fetch; the export-list pin now covers mcp.server. Net prod LOC -3. Was: (a) app/lib/mcp.server.ts:92 declares let makeAdapter = REAL_ADAPTER (:89-90). setAdapterFactory (:94-96) replaces it, and null restores the real one. Nothing else runs at import. (b) The only production reader is callHostedTool (:157, reads it at :200), reached from mcpEndpoint (:508), which app/routes/mcp.$.tsx:152 and :320 call. Writers are tests only: mcp.hosted, mcp.google, mcp.hosted-guards, mcp.knowledge and mcp.reviewer tests, plus tools/assistant-injection.test.ts:111, each pairing set with setAdapterFactory(null) in afterEach. mcp.hosted-guards.test.ts:617-631 must call resetModules and set the seam again on a second module instance. (c) Owner: pass the factory in, e.g. createMcpEndpoint({makeAdapter}) built once in app/routes/mcp.$.tsx with the real factory and per test with a MemoryAdapter (a suggested shape). setAdapterFactory, the let and every afterEach reset could then go. (d) Risk: a test that throws before its reset, or forgets it, leaks a fake adapter into later cases in the same worker. Since the seam is per module instance, a resetModules quietly drops it.
